readings: Using budget lines matched to their event (drop lines with no matching event), first work out for each event the average `remaining` and the average overspend rate, (`spent` − `amount`) ÷ `amount`, across its lines. Then, for each event `status`, average those event-level figures. Return the status, its average remaining, its average overspend rate, and its average remaining divided by the simple mean of the per-status average remaining values, with each status weighted equally. Ignore missing values in every average, and don't round anything.
queries:
WITH event_averages AS (
    SELECT
        e.event_id,
        e.status,
        AVG(b.remaining) AS avg_remaining,
        AVG((b.spent - b.amount) / NULLIF(b.amount, 0)) AS avg_overspend_rate
    FROM event AS e
    JOIN budget AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
    GROUP BY e.event_id, e.status
),
status_averages AS (
    SELECT
        status,
        AVG(avg_remaining) AS avg_remaining,
        AVG(avg_overspend_rate) AS avg_overspend_rate
    FROM event_averages
    GROUP BY status
)
SELECT
    status,
    avg_remaining,
    avg_overspend_rate,
    avg_remaining / (SELECT AVG(avg_remaining) FROM status_averages) AS relative_avg_remaining
FROM status_averages;
